intro: Region boundaries reveal where neighboring pixels receive different class labels. Mark both sides of each local disagreement.
task: Return a boolean map marking pixels with at least one differently labeled four-connected in-bounds neighbor.
requirements: labels is a matrix of integer class IDs 0..1000000. Four-connected means above, below, left and right, excluding diagonals.
Treat positions outside the image as absent, not as background. A uniform image therefore has no boundary pixels, including at its outer edge.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Vertical split
examples.output:
[[False, True, True], [False, True, True]]
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Uniform region
examples.output:
[[False, False, False], [False, False, False], [False, False, False]]
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Single pixel
examples.output:

(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Compare adjacent rows and adjacent columns, marking both members of each unequal pair.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Do not wrap around the image when checking an edge.

explanation: A boundary map converts a region labeling into local transitions. Marking both sides avoids selecting an arbitrary foreground class and works for multiple semantic classes.

The neighborhood and outside-image convention are part of the definition. Diagonal-only contact does not count here, and the image border becomes a boundary only when an actual in-bounds neighbor differs.
